html:
On 17 December 1907 an assembly of monks, officials and leading families at Punakha chose Ugyen Wangchuck as the first hereditary king of Bhutan, founding the Wangchuck dynasty that still reigns.

Since the death of the Zhabdrung in the 17th century, Bhutan had been run by regents and torn by feuds between regional governors. Ugyen Wangchuck, governor of Trongsa, won the last civil war in 1885 and helped the British on their expedition to Tibet in 1904, which won him British backing.

His successors kept Bhutan independent while India grew around it. Jigme Dorji Wangchuck opened the country, Jigme Singye Wangchuck coined Gross National Happiness, and in 2008 the kings gave up absolute power under the Constitution of Bhutan.
